bug_report_content: {"id":1101,"status":"Fixed","summary":"Erroneous optimization in ADVANCED_OPTIMIZATIONS mode","labels":["Type-Defect","Priority-Medium"],"stars":0,"commentCount":17,"comments":[{"id":0,"commenterId":3597220718081656524,"content":" What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. Create a file input.js with the following "minimal" test case: window["anchor"] = function (obj, modifiesProp) { return (function (saved) { return modifiesProp(obj) + saved; })(obj["prop"]); } 2. Compile it with: java -jar .../build/compiler.jar \ --compilation_level ADVANCED_OPTIMIZATIONS \ --warning_level VERBOSE \ --externs window.js \ --js input.js \ --js_output_file output.js 3. That's all! What is the expected output? window.foo=function(a,b){var HOLD=a.prop;return b(a)+HOLD}; What do you see instead? window.foo=function(a,b){return b(a)+a.prop}; Note how this is semantically very different if modifiesProp/b (whose semantics are unknown to the compiler) side-effects a.prop. The evaluation order of + is well-defined in EcmaScript 5, but even then, this happens even if one substitutes the , (comma) operator. What version of the product are you using? On what operating system? Git HEAD commit 4a62ee4bca02169dd77a6f26ed64a624b3f05f95 Author: Chad Killingsworth <chadkillingsworth@missouristate.edu> Date: Wed Sep 25 14:52:28 2013 -0500 Add history.state to html5 externs on Linux.","timestamp":1380185999,"attachments":[]},{"id":1,"commenterId":3597220718081656524,"content":"I had another look at this, and have cooked up the attached patch, which *seems* safe (as it only disables optimizations), but wreaks havoc in the inliner's test suite. Disabling "direct call node" inlining on Node.mayHaveSideEffects() may seem a bit drastic, but a downstream pass still performs inlining—while introducing the required temp!—on my small test case. Not sure if/when that pass is activated, though, so the change may have a more dramatic effect on some code bases. Unfortunately, I lack the time to study the innards of Closure and sift through these failures; it would be great if somebody familiar with the compiler could comment on the next steps to undertake. Cheers, Damien Diederen","timestamp":1380207158,"attachments":[{"id":11010001000,"fileName":"0001-Do-not-directly-replace-a-call-where-return-may-have.patch","fileSize":1382}]},{"id":2,"commenterId":-5060162230523776870,"content":"ouch, thanks for the report. The change in the patch is overly aggressive: we don't need to do this if there aren't any arguments or all of the arguments are literals or otherwise can't be side-effected. If you want to try your hand at a better patch: change "canInlineReferenceDirectly" to check if the function body has side-effects and if it does back out if any of the arguments can be side-effected (NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected)","timestamp":1380240692,"attachments":[]},{"id":3,"commenterId":3597220718081656524,"content":"Hi John, Thanks for the suggestions! I had a stab at fixing this in a less impactful way (patch attached), and am now down to eight failing tests; here is a quick/preliminary analysis: 1. testInlineFunctions6: Now introduces extra temps; 2. testInlineFunctions22: Idem; 3. testInlineFunctions23: Idem; 4. testDoubleInlining1: The argument is possibly modified, but in a tail position; 5. testNoInlineIfParametersModified8: The serialized results match, but the test-generated tree includes an additional BLOCK for some reason; 6. testNoInlineIfParametersModified9: Idem; 7. testIssue1101: My own test; same extra BLOCK; 8. testBug4944818: Haven't looked into it. Feel free to write down further clues that you may have, in case I manage to have another look at this before your team gets to it.
